# The secret merge driver works on the sealed objects git hands it (%O/%A/%B),
# not on the revealed plaintext - so a merge must succeed even when the secret was
# never revealed on disk. Here we drop the revealed file before merging; the driver
# decrypts the objects, produces the merged plaintext, and the finalize verifies.

sesam-repo admin base.txt ours.txt theirs.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt secret.txt
exec sesam add secret.txt --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

exec git checkout -b ours
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt secret.txt
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: first line'

exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt secret.txt
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: last line'

# Drop the revealed plaintext so the merge must run purely from sealed objects.
exec git checkout ours
exec sesam clean
! exists secret.txt

! exec git merge theirs

# The driver decrypted the objects and produced the merged revealed file.
exists secret.txt
grep 'first = OURS' secret.txt
grep 'last = THEIRS' secret.txt

exec git commit --no-edit
exec sesam verify

-- base.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = BASE

-- ours.txt --
first = OURS
middle = BASE
last = BASE

-- theirs.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = THEIRS
